basis: Developmental delay and intellectual disability in 5/5; callosal abnormalities support CNS involvement. Feeding difficulty and constipation do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Corneal dyskeratosis, palmoplantar keratoderma and laryngeal dyskeratosis define the syndrome; visual impairment and nail dystrophy support eye and skin disease.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability and structural brain abnormalities. Hypotonia, feeding difficulty and constipation do not establish additional organ damage.
Benign neoplasm originating in the retina; retinal location belongs to the ocular axis.
Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy; neurologic deterioration and cardiomyopathy each frequent (30-79%). Frequent visual impairment omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Corticospinal tract degeneration causes spastic paraplegia and weakness. Urinary urgency and pes cavus are occasional; weakness does not establish primary muscle damage.
Recurrent complete hydatidiform mole is a gestational trophoblastic disorder confined to reproductive and obstetric tissues.
Familial structural deformity of the foot and associated lower-limb locomotor tissues.
Coloboma, cleft lip/palate and intellectual disability define syndrome; hearing loss in 10/11. Hematuria alone does not establish direct renal damage.
Benign vascular neoplasm composed of cavernous blood-vessel spaces. Anatomical sites vary across subtypes; it is not a blood-cell neoplasm.
Defining CNS and cervico-occipital skeletal malformations; gastroschisis and cardiovascular malformations each frequent (30-79%). Renal agenesis is occasional.
Inherited impairment of cerebral face recognition; this is higher-order visual processing dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye disease.
Malignant neoplasm arising in an extrahepatic bile duct, which belongs to the hepatic axis. Smooth-muscle histology does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Preeclampsia is defined by hypertension with proteinuria or other organ dysfunction; vascular endothelial and renal glomerular injury are characteristic. Eclampsia is a minority.
Cerebellar atrophy and ataxia in 5/5. Dysphagia and abnormal saccades reflect neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated intrinsic gastrointestinal or ocular damage.
Aniridia and patellar aplasia or hypoplasia define the syndrome; cataract and glaucoma remain within the ocular axis.
Intrahepatic cholestasis directly impairs liver function. Villous atrophy relates to parenteral feeding rather than direct cholestatic injury; splenomegaly alone is insufficient.
B-cell lymphoma arising in the thyroid: endocrine-gland location, hematologic cell lineage and lymphoma mechanism.
Hypothalamic hamartoma, pituitary dysfunction and skeletal defects define PHS; anal atresia 30-79%. Airway, renal, ocular, ear and nail anomalies omitted at cap.
Carcinoma originating in a salivary gland. Neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease or a metabolic disorder.
Stage I carcinoma confined to the uterine body, potentially involving cervical glands; these reproductive tissues have no axis.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss in 5/5. Myopia in 3/5 does not establish that this hearing disorder directly damages the eye.
Inherited dopamine-synthesis defect causes dystonia and parkinsonism. Oculogyric crises, ptosis and dystonic foot posturing do not establish independent eye or muscle damage.
Persistent asymptomatic blood eosinophilia; the definition excludes eosinophil-mediated organ injury. Restrictive cardiomyopathy ancestry does not establish cardiac involvement.
Benign fibroblastic neoplasm of fascia and subcutaneous soft tissue. Local inflammatory infiltrates do not make this an immune-mediated disease.
